area.title: Animal identification details
area.scope: The identification details page: which species need identifying and with which identifiers (ear tag, passport, microchip, tattoo, germinal donor and dates), entering, saving and removing animals, the per-line count and its cap, identifier validation, the selected-commodities summary on the page, and the per-animal permanent address fields the real frontend keeps on this page today. Stops at the permanent address page in consignment parties.

sources.role: the owner's decisions: outranks every other source. Search boxes use the real frontend's accessible component with MDM's entries. JavaScript behaviour follows the toolbox rule with graceful degradation; JavaScript-only prototype behaviour, pop-ups included, waits on design in its own theme. Commodity catalogue and search wait on MDM; transporter management waits on requirements; the INS dashboard's summary information waits on its requirements. The overview, review, declaration and confirmation are set-owned, and shared parts change add-only. Where plants has the same page or behaviour, the same increment changes it. Each notification list is reframed in its own frontend. The report groups work as ready or blocked. Claims marked as the orchestrator's apply Sam's principles and are not his rulings; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-templates covers templates and the dashboard narrowing.

claims.statement: Sam rules that the prototype's search and autocomplete controls are not accessible and not production grade, because they are AI-generated prototype code rather than GDS components.
claims.quote: Now we need to be really careful here because the prototype isn't accessible. It's not using some GDS stuff. It's using prototype thrown up by AI stuff. ... the prototype isn't necessarily production-grade with its solution.

claims.statement: Sam rules that for a search box the precedence is not 'prototype always wins': the component used may be the one already in the real frontends, where it has been deemed accessible.
claims.quote: only use a version of auto complete or search or whatever that has been deemed accessible and meets our requirements. If it has been, the sort of precedence needs to be a little bit different than prototype always wins. In terms of the component being used, it might be the one that's actually in the frontend or frontends.

claims.statement: Sam says the content of a search dropdown (such as which countries a country dropdown holds) is not settled by 'the frontend is correct' and may need more input.

claims.statement: Sam rules that the prototype's JavaScript behaviour is not GDS compliant and is not to be blindly replicated by adding lots of JavaScript to the frontend, for accessibility and maintainability reasons.
claims.quote: the prototype is doing stuff with JavaScript that is not GDS compliant. This isn't stuff that can just be blindly replicated by chucking a tonne of JavaScript in the frontend. ... 'Do things like add all this JavaScript stuff for accessibility concerns and maintainability concerns.'

claims.statement: Sam rules that GDS components are the toolbox, and where one is not available another tested, accessible government library (such as Ministry of Justice or Scottish Government) is used.
claims.quote: We really try to strictly head here to GDS components as a toolbox, and where that's not available, use other government libraries like a Ministry of Justice or a Scottish Government component that has been tested and meets accessibility requirements.

claims.statement: Sam rules there is a graceful degradation requirement: CSS and JavaScript may enhance behaviour, but every page must work without JavaScript, so the prototype's way of doing things may not be possible or wanted in the real service.
claims.quote: We've got a graceful degradation requirement on this, like any other GDS project, which means you can use things like CSS and JavaScript to enhance behaviour, but you need graceful degradation. It needs to be able to work without JavaScript, and that means that the way things are done in the prototype may not be possible or even desired in the real thing.

claims.statement: Sam rules that, as a pre-step for these increments, three questions are answered: is it possible with off-the-shelf GDS; if not, with other complementary off-the-shelf components; if not, why is the atypical thing strongly required. At that point it goes back to design to push back.
claims.quote: Almost as a pre-step for some of these increments, we need to get answers to that stuff: - Is it possible using off-the-shelf GDS? - If it isn't, is it using available, off-the-shelf, other complementary components? - If it isn't, why is this atypical thing strongly required? At that point, we go back to design and say, 'Come on, we don't need this.'

claims.statement: A behaviour the prototype gives with JavaScript is built only if it passes these tests in order: GOV.UK Frontend's components and patterns first; then another tested government library (Ministry of Justice, HMRC, Scottish Government); otherwise it goes back to design, which must say why it is strongly needed.
claims.quote: GOV.UK Frontend's components and patterns are used first. Where they have nothing, another tested government library is used, such as the Ministry of Justice's, HMRC's or the Scottish Government's. Where neither has anything, the behaviour goes back to design, which must say why it is strongly needed.
claims.note: Marked 'Sam (point 3)'. HMRC is named in claim 5 but not in Sam's quote, which names Ministry of Justice and Scottish Government only; the examples are illustrative ('like').

claims.statement: Nothing other than a DR1 judgement on the same difference or a real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides the prototype.
claims.quote: Only a DR1 judgement or a real constraint the prototype can't express (persistence, validation, auth, cross-service behaviour) overrides it.
claims.note: New. In particular, what a real service does today is not on its own a reason to depart from the prototype.

claims.statement: Questions for people are kept to a minimum.
claims.quote: Decisions: keep questions for people to a minimum.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: A question for people is raised only when a difference is truly exceptional and neither the prototype default nor a DR1 judgement settles it.
claims.quote: Raise one only when a difference is truly exceptional and neither the default nor DR1 settles it.
claims.note: New. Both conditions must hold. 'The default' is read as the prototype-wins default from the Precedence paragraph.

claims.statement: Increments are grouped into themes, and the themes are drawn from the evidence.
claims.quote: Themes: group the increments into themes based on the evidence.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Each theme's boundary is set by the code it touches.
claims.quote: Draw the boundaries by the code each one touches
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Themes can be built in parallel on separate machines without pull requests that conflict with each other.
claims.quote: so themes can be built in parallel on separate machines without conflicting PRs.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: The ruling's DR1 paragraph has an elision marked [...]: what the omitted words said about the DR1 parity backlog is not recorded.
The ruling does not say what makes a difference 'truly exceptional', so when a question for people is warranted is left open.

The ruling limits DR1 use to clashes between 'the real frontend' and the prototype; it does not say which frontend that is, or whether DR1 judgements apply to differences in the INS frontend, the backends or other repos.
The ruling does not say which override wins when a DR1 judgement and a real constraint the prototype cannot express point different ways on the same difference.
The ruling does not say what a real service does where a real constraint overrides the prototype: whether it keeps today's behaviour or matches the prototype as closely as the constraint allows.
The ruling does not say whether a feature or behaviour a real service has that Design Release 2.1 does not show at all counts as a difference to remove, or is left alone.
The ruling does not say what to do where the code two themes need to touch overlaps, so no boundary keeps their pull requests from conflicting.

claims.statement: A remove request for a position that does not exist is ignored; when the last saved animal of a species is removed, the species' identification record is deleted.
Identification details are stored per species as a list of entries, each entry holding one value per identifier field id.

Identification is complete for the notification when, for every selected species with identifier fields, every required entry is saved and complete (for germinal products, the one entry exists); a species with fields but no animals counts as incomplete.

Minimum-identifier rule for submitting: identification details are optional when only one species is selected; when more than one species is selected and any has identifier fields, each species with fields needs at least one complete entry (for germinal products, a saved entry).
claims.note: The rule is used by the review/submit readiness check (routes.js:4989-4993, read for context): "Animal identifiers are optional unless multiple species are selected, in which case at least one identifier is required per species." Species without identifier fields always pass. The page itself shows no message about this rule; the review and submit parts own how a failure is shown.

claims.statement: The animal identification page can be opened and posted at any point in the journey: its origin, commodity, import-reason and consignment-details guards all return false, so it never redirects a user who has skipped earlier pages.

claims.statement: On Save and continue or a soft save, every single-animal and germinal species' values are written to the session before the errors are shown, including a value that failed validation; so an invalid collection or production date stays saved, and a germinal species counts as identified, if the user leaves by the back link instead of correcting it.
claims.note: Inferred: saveActiveAnimalIdentifiersFromBody saves values unconditionally after collecting errors, unlike the per-panel save, which returns before saving when there are errors (12465-12473).

claims.statement: A per-panel save that fails validation saves nothing; in practice it never fails, because only germinal fields have rules and germinal panels have no panel save button.
claims.note: Inferred from the live-animal identifier fields carrying no type or maxLength, and germinal panels having totalAnimals 1, which hides the panel button.

claims.statement: Lowering a species' number of animals, or removing the species, does not remove identification entries already saved; the saved-animals table keeps listing every complete saved entry, so it can show more animals than the new number.

claims.statement: Identifier errors are held in the session and shown whenever the page is opened, until a successful save, Save and continue or Remove clears them, so reloading the page after an error shows the error summary again.

sources.role: what exists today and what has already been ruled

claims.statement: The animal identification page lives at the journey path commodities/identification.
The page heading is "Identification details".
claims.quote: title: 'Identification details',

claims.statement: The page shows a section caption above the heading.
claims.quote: {{ sectionCaption(caption) }}
claims.note: The caption's text comes from the shared section-caption helper, outside this part.

claims.statement: Below the heading, inset text says: "You must add all animal identification details before the consignment arrives at the port of entry."
claims.quote: 'You must add all animal identification details before the consignment arrives at the port of entry.'

claims.statement: The page's back link goes to the journey hub (the Overview page).
claims.quote: backLink: hubPath(journey.journeyId),

claims.statement: A user reaches the page from the hub's animal identification task row.
claims.quote:
await page
    .getByRole('link', { name: hubCopy.rows.animalIdentification.title })
    .click()
claims.note: The hub row's wording is in the hub copy, another part.

claims.statement: The page only asks about commodity lines whose commodity declares at least one identifier type; a line whose commodity declares none gets no identification card.
There is no free-text identifier fallback: a commodity with no declared identifiers is asked for none.
claims.quote:
// A commodity that declares no identifier is asked for none: design release 1
// has no free-text fallback, so the list is empty and the line gets no panel.

claims.statement: When no commodity line on the notification declares an identifier, the page does not exist for that user: both a GET and a POST to it redirect to the next step of the journey.

Which identifier fields a commodity shows, and in what order, is set by the commodity's own identifier list in the commodity catalogue, filtered by whether the obligation model says each identifier applies to that commodity.
claims.note: The per-commodity identifier lists live in services/commodities, outside this part.

claims.statement: The identifier types the page can ask for are microchip, passport, tattoo, ear tag and horse name.
claims.quote:
typeFields: {
      animalIdentifierMicrochip: {

claims.statement: The microchip field is labelled "Microchip number" with the hint "For example, 900123456789012".
The passport field is labelled "Passport" with the hint "For example, UK123456789".
The tattoo field is labelled "Tattoo" with the hint "For example, AB1234".
The ear tag field is labelled "Ear tag" with the hint "For example, UK123456789012".
The horse name field is labelled "Horse name" and has no hint.
claims.quote: horseName: { label: 'Horse name' }

claims.statement: Identifier fields are plain text inputs with a small bold label and a width of 20 characters.
claims.quote:
label: { text: field.label, classes: "govuk-label--s" },
          hint: field.hint and { text: field.hint },
          classes: "govuk-input--width-20",

claims.statement: Each field's id and name is the field key followed by a hyphen and the commodity line's index, so the first line's ear tag is animalIdentifierEarTag-0.
claims.quote: export const fieldName = (id, index) => `${id}-${index}`

claims.statement: No single identifier is mandatory: each is optional on its own, and the only identifier check besides length is that "Save and add another" with nothing entered anywhere on the page is refused.
claims.quote:
export const identifierChecksFor = (commodity, index) =>
  compose(
    ...scopedFields(commodity).map((field) =>
      maxText(
claims.note: Inferred because the only identifier validators are maxText checks plus the empty-form guard; there is no required check per identifier. Whether the obligation model makes any identifier mandatory for submit is outside this part.

claims.statement: Each identifier value can be at most 58 characters.
claims.quote: const IDENTIFIER_MAX_LENGTH = 58

claims.statement: A microchip longer than 58 characters shows the error "Microchip must be 58 characters or fewer".
claims.quote: animalIdentifierMicrochip: 'Microchip must be 58 characters or fewer',

claims.statement: A passport longer than 58 characters shows the error "Passport must be 58 characters or fewer".
claims.quote: animalIdentifierPassport: 'Passport must be 58 characters or fewer',

claims.statement: A tattoo longer than 58 characters shows the error "Tattoo must be 58 characters or fewer".
claims.quote: animalIdentifierTattoo: 'Tattoo must be 58 characters or fewer',

claims.statement: An ear tag longer than 58 characters shows the error "Ear tag must be 58 characters or fewer".
claims.quote: animalIdentifierEarTag: 'Ear tag must be 58 characters or fewer',

claims.statement: A horse name longer than 58 characters shows the error "Horse name must be 58 characters or fewer".
claims.quote: horseName: 'Horse name must be 58 characters or fewer'

claims.statement: Identifier and address values are trimmed of surrounding whitespace before they are checked and saved.
claims.quote: (payload[fieldName(field.id, index)] ?? '').trim()

claims.statement: Pressing "Save and add another" on a card when nothing has been entered on any card shows the error "Enter at least one identifier for this animal", attached to that card's first identifier field, and saves nothing.
claims.quote: atLeastOneIdentifier: 'Enter at least one identifier for this animal',

claims.statement: Pressing the page's "Save and continue" with nothing entered on any card shows no error and saves no animal record before moving on.
claims.note: Inferred from the empty-form guard firing only for an add action, and append skipping forms that hold no data.

claims.statement: Some commodities also ask for each animal's permanent address; whether a commodity does is decided by the obligation model's applicability for permanentAddress.
claims.quote:
export const permanentAddressApplies = (commodity) =>
  appliesForCommodity('permanentAddress', commodity)
claims.note: The spec shows cat and dog lines get the address block and a cow line does not; it does not check a horse line's address.

claims.statement: Above the permanent address fields, a warning says "Providing a false address is an act of fraud".
claims.quote: warning: 'Providing a false address is an act of fraud',

claims.statement: After the warning the page defines a permanent address: "A permanent address is where an animal:" followed by the bullets "will permanently reside" and "can be checked by the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA)".
claims.quote:
definitionLeadIn: 'A permanent address is where an animal:',
      definitionItems: [
        'will permanently reside',
        'can be checked by the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA)'
      ],

claims.statement: The address fields sit under a small heading "Where will their permanent address be?".
claims.quote: question: 'Where will their permanent address be?'

claims.statement: The fraud warning and definition come before the address question because the reason the address matters (APHA checks it) is what deters an invented one.
claims.quote:
Design release 1 puts the fraud warning and the definition of a
           permanent address above the question, because the reason the
           address matters — APHA checks it — is what stops an invented one.

claims.statement: The permanent address asks for eight fields in this order: name or organisation name, address line 1, address line 2, town or city, county, postcode or Zip code, phone number, email address.
claims.quote:
const ADDRESS_FIELD_ORDER = [
  'nameOrOrganisationName',
  'addressLine1',
  'addressLine2',
  'townOrCity',
  'county',
  'postalOrZipCode',
  'telephoneNumber',
  'emailAddress'
]

claims.statement: The permanent address never asks for a country and has no select list.
claims.quote: permanent address asks for eight fields and never for a country

claims.statement: The first address field is labelled "Name or organisation name", with autocomplete name.
claims.quote: nameOrOrganisationName: 'Name or organisation name',

claims.statement: The address line fields are labelled "Address line 1" and "Address line 2 (optional)", with autocomplete address-line1 and address-line2.
claims.quote:
addressLine1: 'Address line 1',
      addressLine2: 'Address line 2 (optional)',

claims.statement: The town field is labelled "Town or city", two-thirds width, with autocomplete address-level2.
claims.quote: townOrCity: 'Town or city',

claims.statement: The county field is labelled "County (optional)", two-thirds width, with no autocomplete.
claims.quote: county: 'County (optional)',

claims.statement: The postcode field is labelled "Postcode or Zip code", 10 characters wide, with autocomplete postal-code.
claims.quote: postalOrZipCode: 'Postcode or Zip code',

claims.statement: The phone field is labelled "Phone number", is a telephone input 20 characters wide with autocomplete tel, and has the hint "For international numbers include the country code".
claims.quote: telephoneNumber: 'For international numbers include the country code'

claims.statement: The phone field is the only address field with a hint, because a trader giving an address outside the UK would not otherwise know the number will be dialled from the UK.
The email field is labelled "Email address" and is an email input with autocomplete email.
claims.quote: emailAddress: 'Email address'

claims.statement: The permanent address is all or nothing per animal: if any address field is filled in, name or organisation name, address line 1, town or city, postcode or Zip code, phone number and email address all become required; address line 2 and county stay optional.
An animal on an address-bearing commodity can be saved with no permanent address at all, as long as no address field is filled in.

claims.note: Inferred: missing-field errors only fire when some address field is given, and the record is saved without a permanentAddress otherwise. Whether submit later demands the address is the obligation model's call, outside this part.

          'Name or organisation name must be 255 characters or less',

claims.note: Inferred: every address validator is maxText; the copy key is named addressFormat but holds only length messages.

claims.statement: Each card is headed with the commodity name, its commodity code in brackets, a dash and the species, such as "Cow (0102) — Bos taurus"; without a code or species those parts are left out.
claims.note: The example is assembled from the spec's Cow / 0102 / Bos taurus data, not quoted.

claims.statement: Each card has an anchor id identification-card-N, where N is the commodity line's index.
claims.quote: anchor: `identification-card-${index}`,

claims.statement: Every card has a "Change number of animals" link, with the card title as visually hidden text, that goes to the consignment details page carrying the change context.
claims.quote: changeAnimalCount: 'Change number of animals',

claims.statement: The Change number of animals link sits beside the counter because the counter is the only place on the page that mentions the number of animals the trader is held to.
claims.quote:
// The card counter is the only place the declared animal count appears, so
// every card carries the route back to the page that sets it.
claims.note: The same comment says Design release 1 puts a bare link on every panel with no change context, but the controller's href does carry change context (kit.withChangeContext). Recorded as written; the reconciler should note the mismatch.

claims.statement: While the line still has animals to record, the card shows a counter heading "Enter details for {species} {next} of {count}", where next is the number of saved records plus one and count is the declared number of animals.
claims.quote:
counter: (species, next, cap) =>
      `Enter details for ${species} ${next} of ${cap}`,

claims.statement: When the line has no declared number of animals, the counter reads "Enter details for {species}" with no count.
claims.quote: counterNoCap: (species) => `Enter details for ${species}`,

claims.statement: The number of animal records a line can hold is capped at the line's declared number of animals.
claims.quote:
// "Save and add another" pressed against a card already at its cap — a
// stale form racing the engine-enforced cardinality link.
claims.note: Inferred: the cap comes from state.collectionCapAt on animalIdentifiers, and the counter and spec tie it to the number of animals; the cardinality link itself is in the obligation model, another part.

claims.statement: When a line holds as many records as its declared number of animals, the card hides the entry form and shows "You have entered details for all {count} {species} animals. Remove a record if you need to replace it."
claims.quote:
allEntered: (cap, species) =>
      `You have entered details for all ${cap} ${species} animals. Remove a record if you need to replace it.`,

claims.statement: When a line holds more records than its declared number of animals, the card hides the entry form and shows "This commodity line lists {count} {species} animals but you have entered details for {records}. Remove {excess} to continue."
claims.quote:
overCount: (cap, species, entered, overBy) =>
      `This commodity line lists ${cap} ${species} animals but you have entered details for ${entered}. Remove ${overBy} to continue.`,

claims.statement: The in-card save button reads "Save and add another" while more than one animal is still outstanding on the line, or when the line has no declared count.
claims.quote: saveAndAddAnother: 'Save and add another',

claims.statement: On the last animal still outstanding, the in-card save button reads "Save and finish".
claims.quote: return cap - records === 1 ? copy.saveAndFinish : copy.saveAndAddAnother

claims.statement: A line declaring one animal gets no in-card save button: the page's own Save and continue captures that one record.
claims.quote:
// A line of one animal gets no button of its own — there is nothing to add
// after this record, so the page's own Save and continue captures it.

claims.statement: The in-card save button is a secondary button.
claims.quote: classes: "govuk-button--secondary",

claims.statement: Pressing an in-card save button saves the animal and reloads the identification page (keeping any change context) rather than moving on.
Any save on the page, whichever button is pressed, saves one new animal record for every card whose entry form holds data, not only the card whose button was pressed.
Validation runs across every open card on any save, and if any card has an error nothing is saved and the page re-renders with every entered value kept.
After a successful page save (not an in-card add), the user goes to the next step the journey flow gives for this page.
claims.quote: return h.redirect(await kit.nextTarget(request, page, savedScope))
claims.note: Where nextTarget leads (hub or check answers in change mode) is the flow's business, another part. The spec shows Save and continue returns to the Overview.

claims.statement: The page ends on the shared journey save actions, whose primary button is "Save and continue".
claims.quote: {{ saveActions(hubHref, copy = sharedCopy.saveActions) }}

claims.statement: Pressing Enter in a field submits the page as its default finish action, not as an in-card add, through a hidden "Save and finish" button placed first in the form.
claims.quote: <button type="submit" name="action" value="finish" class="govuk-visually-hidden" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">{{ copy.saveAndFinish }}</button>
claims.note: Inferred from a hidden first submit button with value finish: browsers use the first submit button for implicit submission.

claims.statement: The form carries a CSRF crumb and a concurrency token on every submission.
claims.quote:
<input type="hidden" name="crumb" value="{{ crumb }}" />
    <input type="hidden" name="concurrencyToken" value="{{ concurrencyToken }}" />

claims.statement: If an add is submitted for a card already at its cap (for example from a stale form), nothing is saved and the page shows "You have already entered details for all {count} animals — remove a record before adding another", linked to that card.
claims.quote:
capReached: (cap) =>
        `You have already entered details for all ${cap} animals — remove a record before adding another`

claims.statement: If saving a record fails because the line has reached its cap at save time, the same cap-reached error is shown against that card and the page re-renders from the saved state.
The error summary uses the shared error-summary title, links each field error to its field id and each card-level error to the card's anchor.
Each animal record is saved under its commodity line with the identifier values entered for that commodity's fields.
claims.quote:
['commodityLines', index, 'animalIdentifiers'],
      unitFromForm(form)

claims.statement: When a permanent address is given, it is saved on the animal record as a name plus an address holding address line 1, address line 2, town or city, county, postcode or Zip code, phone number and email address.
The animal record's microchip, passport, tattoo, ear tag, horse name and permanent address each feed their own obligation in the notification model, per animal within each commodity line.
claims.quote:

claims.statement: Once a line has at least one saved animal, the card shows a table of saved animals above the entry form.

The saved-animals table's columns are "Animal", then one column per identifier the commodity declares (whether filled in or not), then "Permanent address" where the commodity takes one, then a visually hidden "Actions" column.
claims.quote:
animalColumn: 'Animal',
      permanentAddressColumn: 'Permanent address',

claims.statement: The identifier column headings are "Microchip", "Passport", "Tattoo", "Ear tag" and "Horse name".
claims.quote:
animalIdentifierMicrochip: 'Microchip',

  // wording Design release 1 has not settled here.

claims.quote: (id === PERMANENT_ADDRESS ? unit.permanentAddress?.name : unit[id]) ?? ''

claims.statement: Each saved row ends with a "Remove" button styled as a link, with visually hidden text "animal {n}".

claims.statement: Removing an animal is a form POST, never a GET; it deletes that one record and reloads the identification page with the change context kept.

// crumb travels with it and no GET can trigger it.

claims.statement: A remove request naming a line or record that does not exist is refused with a 400 Bad Request before anything is deleted.
Removing an animal from a full line reopens the entry form for that line.
claims.quote: blocks a count drop below saved records and reopens after removal

claims.statement: Above the cards, a table captioned "Selected commodities" lists every commodity line on the consignment, including lines that get no identification card.

claims.statement: Below the summary, an "Add another commodity" link goes to the commodity search question carrying the change context, and shows whenever the page shows.
claims.quote: addAnotherCommodity: 'Add another commodity',

claims.statement: The animal identification page is at /live-animals/notifications/{id}/commodities/identification and is headed (h1) "Identification details".
The identification page asks for an animal's "Ear tag" and "Passport".
Each saved animal is a row of the card's table, keyed by species and number (such as "Bos taurus 1"), under identifier column headers.
claims.quote:
// A saved animal is one row of the card's table, keyed by its species and
  // number — "Bos taurus 1".

claims.statement: The identification card's own button reads "Save and add another" while animals remain on the line, and "Save and finish" on the last outstanding animal.
Test 'renders the page controls' proves the identification page shows its heading, Ear tag, Passport and Save and continue, and that a line of one animal shows no "Save and add another" button.
Test 'leaves the ear tag empty on load' proves the Ear tag field starts blank.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/pages/animal-identification.spec.ts:18 'leaves the ear tag empty on load'
claims.quote: await expect(animalsPages.animalIdentification.earTag).toHaveValue('');

claims.statement: Test 'accepts a valid ear tag' proves ear tag UK123456789012 saves without an error.
claims.quote: await animalsPages.animalIdentification.earTag.fill('UK123456789012');

claims.statement: Saving the identification page with an ear tag returns the user to the overview.
No page test submits the identification page empty or with a malformed ear tag or passport, so whether an identifier is required, any format rule, and their error messages are not proven.

claims.statement: The trace never shows validation of an identifier's format: no invalid ear tag, passport, microchip or tattoo was submitted, so any format rule and its error copy is unseen.

The trace never shows a horse line or any other species with its own identifier set, so the commodities that get a 'Horse name' field (asserted absent for cats) and their form are unseen.
The trace never shows a consignment with two or more identifier-bearing lines, so how multiple cards stack on the page is unseen.

The trace never shows what happens to identifier records or the CPH number when the triggering commodity line is removed.
